sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Purpose and imports
sections.what: The header says each adapter parses source files into facts and never invents values. It brings in the shared incident and sport types.
sections.why: Protects the app from showing numbers that were never in the source.
sections.watch_out: The no-invented-values rule is a promise, not a check, so each parser must be reviewed.

sections.name: ParsedEvent, SourcePending
sections.title: Shape of one parsed match or race
sections.what: Defines the record each parser returns: where it came from, its sport, competition, season, name, start time, venue, teams or cars, outcome facts and incidents. Also defines the pending record.
sections.why: One shared shape means every sport feeds the same storage and screens.
sections.watch_out: The outcome field accepts any keys, so a sport can store values that nothing here checks.

summary: The shared shape of the data every source adapter returns, plus the shape of a pending source.
purpose: It defines the common format that lets matches from different sports be stored and shown the same way.
why: One shared format keeps the storage and the screens simple.
how: It defines a parsed event with its source, sport, competition, season, name, start time, venue, teams or cars, outcome, and incidents. It also defines the pending record with its reason.
inputs: Not applicable: this file only defines types.
outputs: Not applicable: this file only defines types.
risks: The outcome field accepts any keys, so each sport can store different values and nothing here checks them.
debug: If a type error appears, compare the field names with what the adapter returns. Because this file has no logic, bugs are usually in the adapter that builds the data.
